stories.headline: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
stories.script: Our lead story today. Hundreds of servers running Artex, a penetration testing tool, were left open on the internet, letting anyone reach the hacking tool, TechCrunch reports, citing security researchers.
stories.whyThisMatters: Hundreds of servers running Artex, a penetration testing tool, were left open on the internet, letting anyone reach the hacking tool, TechCrunch reports, citing security researchers.

stories.headline: Activists break into building site of Microsoft datacentre in Amsterdam
stories.script: Also today. Activists have forced their way into the construction site of a Microsoft datacentre in Amsterdam, the Guardian reports. Members of Geef Tegengas, a Dutch direct action group, scuffled with police as they entered the Westpoort site. Some climbed a crane, set off flares and attached helium balloons to machinery. Other protests took place outside the fence and in other parts of Europe, part of growing opposition to the social and environmental toll of the AI boom.
stories.whyThisMatters: Activists have forced their way into the construction site of a Microsoft datacentre in Amsterdam, the Guardian reports.
keyPoints: Activists break into building site of Microsoft datacentre in Amsterdam
The Guardian

stories.headline: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
stories.script: In other news. Crusoe, the Denver-based data center developer recently valued at 30.9 billion dollars, confirmed on Friday it has sold an unfinished project in southeastern Wyoming to Google, TechCrunch reports. Crusoe had previously tried without success to sign Google as a customer for the site, and Google reportedly voiced worries about costs and timelines under Crusoe's management. Crusoe first announced the project last year alongside Tallgrass, an infrastructure firm backed by Blackstone, with ambitions to reach 10 gigawatts of capacity. Google did not reveal the purchase price but said it plans to invest 17 billion dollars building out the campus. The sale underscores the struggle independent developers face in completing huge projects on schedule and on budget, amid difficulties obtaining equipment and power.
stories.whyThisMatters: Crusoe, the Denver-based data center developer recently valued at 30.9 billion dollars, confirmed on Friday it has sold an unfinished project in southeastern Wyoming to Google, TechCrunch reports.

stories.script: Turning to India. The US Department of Agriculture will apply an AI tool to its crop production report due on November 10, according to The Economic Times. Under Secretary Scott Hutchins said officials concluded the tool would have caught mistakes found in the department's September corn figures.

stories.headline: Three men charged in US with using AI to impersonate CEOs and steal millions
stories.script: Around the world. Three foreign nationals have been arrested and charged in the United States with allegedly using artificial intelligence to pose as company chief executives and lawyers, stealing more than 100 million dollars, the Guardian reports. An indictment unsealed by the Justice Department names Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan and Guy Sheetrit. Prosecutors in the southern district of New York say the men manipulated the voices and images of executives and attorneys at several firms, persuading staff to transfer large sums. Soall and Hazan were detained in Spain over the summer, and Sheetrit was arrested in the United Kingdom in September.

stories.headline: Lanarkshire AI datacentre to fully rely on National Grid despite renewables claim
stories.script: In other news. DataVita, the company behind a major AI datacentre project near Glasgow, has conceded the development will run entirely on power from the National Grid, despite earlier promises of renewable supply, the Guardian reports. The firm, seen as central to Britain's AI strategy, had pledged that the Lanarkshire scheme would take 1GW from green sources, comparable to a small nuclear reactor or the country's largest windfarm. When questioned by the Guardian, DataVita said the arrangement depended on commercial agreements, planning, grid and consent processes. It has since quietly changed the plan, now describing the site, near Chapelhall outside Airdrie, as fully grid served. It says solar and wind farms might be connected later.

stories.headline: Tech companies face mounting child safety lawsuits while pushing AI into schools
stories.script: Turning to the United States. Technology companies are facing a growing wave of child safety litigation even as they push artificial intelligence into classrooms, CNBC reports. Snap has reached a confidential settlement in a case alleging its technology caused serious psychological harm to two teenagers, after Meta, TikTok and YouTube earlier settled with the same plaintiffs. This week, Google was sued by parents who say their child experienced a psychological crisis after conversations with the Gemini chatbot inside Google Classroom. The concerns are mounting as AI firms chase trillion-dollar valuations and large internet companies spend heavily on advanced models for schools. Developmental psychologist Kate Blocker said engagement-driven features can harm users, calling for "broader systemic changes in tech design."
stories.whyThisMatters: Technology companies are facing a growing wave of child safety litigation even as they push artificial intelligence into classrooms, CNBC reports.
keyPoints: Tech companies face mounting child safety lawsuits while pushing AI into schools
